dsh-a2a-server
Inbound A2A protocol server for DeepSeek Harness.
Publish an Agent Card, accept tasks from any compliant peer.
Everything is a plugin — this is one.
English · 简体中文
A community plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.

`dsh-a2a-server` makes a DeepSeek Harness
agent reachable over the A2A (Agent2Agent) protocol. It
se

rves an Agent Card at a well-known URI and implements the **v1.0 JSON-RPC
binding**, so any complian

t peer that knows the deployment's URL can discover the
agent and submit tasks to it.

The plugin is **inbound only**: it never connects to another agent. There is no
client, no peer dire

ctory, and no A2A subagent provider. It is a transport
adapter over `ctx.agents`, not a capability s

y, and no A2A subagent provider. It is a transport
adapter over `ctx.agents`, not a capability seam.

For a local configuration UI and cross-network access, use the companion
Talk2MyAgent setup guide.

ee the deployment and migration guide
for visitor permissions, automatic briefings, private owner ac

nd migration guide
for visitor permissions, automatic briefings, private owner access and Tailscale.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory and appends this
bundle to `dsh.profile.b

undles`, because the package declares `dsh.bundle`.
Since DSH v0.2.1-alpha.1, `--profile` must come

before any pnpm arguments —
the forms above already do.
To work from a checkout instead, point it at the directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Requirement | Supplied by |

| `ctx.agents` | `dsh-base` |
| `ctx.credentials` | `dsh-base` |
| `ctx.webServer` | **`dsh-web-app`

** |
| `ctx.tools` and `ctx.systemPrompt` | required visitor tool and prompt isolation services |
|
`ctx.sessionProjections` (optional) | composition; exposes task lifecycle projections |

The plugin stays PENDING until all required services exist. `ctx.webServer`
ships in `dsh-web-app` r

ather than `dsh-base`, so a `headless` profile needs
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` mounted befor

e this bundle serves anything.
`dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` prints the composed rows.
### Upgrading to 0.4.1

Version 0.4.1 requires DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. Stop the agent, install
`dsh-a2a-server@0.4.1` int

o its existing profile, then restart it. Owner RPC and
monitoring now use authenticated local IPC; u

pdate the companion Portal as well.
Visitors retain chat and scoped workspace reads, while other too

ls are denied.
An empty `trustedPeers: []` denies all visitors. Task results persist across
restart
within the configured retention window.

The current Talk2MyAgent Portal
configures default-on hourly briefings with one persistent switch. T

he plugin
alone does not enable automatic briefing without its `briefing` configuration.
Portal auto
matically prepares Microsandbox for per-visitor isolation. Public data is copied read-only, excludin
g `node_modules`; private files persist on independent visitor disks. Idle VMs pause after 30 second
s and stop after 10 minutes. Existing standalone configurations keep their selected execution mode;
installing the plugin alone does not enable a VM. See the sandbox guide and 0.4.1 release notes.
### Public visitors (0.4.1)
The companion Portal can opt into public access, off by default. Clients send normally; an explicit
pre-execution 401 challenge lets the updated skill register, save a server-issued credential and con
tinue the original message once. The local server enforces five accepted messages across conversatio
ns and restarts, then asks the visitor to contact the owner for access. This is an optional RPC exte
nsion, not a redirect or automatic behavior of every A2A client. See the client flow, quota rules an
d credential storage. Existing invited peers retain their access; when public admission is enabled,
its issued identities are admitted independently of `trustedPeers`.

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**A task is an interval, not a turn.** One submitted message may span several
turns if tools queue m

ore work, so settlement uses three hooks:
`agent/inbox/claimed` binds the message to a turn, `turn/e

nd` records that turn's
ending, and `agent.whenIdle()` settles once the whole agent is quiet.

**Task state lives in the session log.** Lifecycle transitions are `a2a/task`
events; a projection u

nit folds them into the read model. The terminal edge
carries the committed output, so the fold serv

es the answer without reaching
back into message history.

**Residency is explicit.** HTTP has no connection lifetime, so each `contextId`
maps to an Activatio

n evicted when idle. Private checkpoints retain task results
and conversation history; cold restorat
ion creates a new harness session.
